main_results.scope: A compact complex surface admits at most two smooth connected-fibre holomorphic fibrations over curves of genus at least two, up to base biholomorphism, under the stated universal classical inputs.
Non-isotriviality is witnessed by two actual compact fibre curves with no biholomorphism; Kodaira base hyperbolicity is a separate input to the corollary.
Two inequivalent smooth fibrations give a finite surjective map to the product of their bases.
The classical zero-degree consequence of a holomorphic connection is an explicit general input.
Equal derivative ramification divisors give equal pullback metrics and local isometry graphs, including ramified centres.
Critical components carry cyclic normal charts, unramified restrictions, Jacobian order n−1 and negative normal-cocycle degree.

The local second projection has the stated derivative and rank criterion; the Zaal application obtains a nonsubmersion from raw construction data without assuming connected second fibres or assigning total degree to a component.
A third fibration is disjoint from a critical component or shares its tangency, supporting the common-index construction.
The disjoint and common-tangency cases contradict negative normal degree, using actual splittings and cyclic averaging.
The disjoint and common-tangency cases contradict negative normal degree, using actual splittings and cyclic averaging.
Every hyperbolic third fibration of a finite unramified product cover factors through one projection; it need not be smooth.
Pushforward of actual punctured bundle sections defines the cyclic representation used for averaging, principal-part cancellation and holomorphic extension, under generic analytic/bundle inputs.

main_results.scope: Three pair normal atlases with orders at least two on a hyperbolic curve force compatible Taylor coefficients and a tangent holomorphic connection, contradicting its degree under the stated degree-theory inputs.
The two projections of a product of hyperbolic compact curves are smooth connected-fibre fibrations and inequivalent by base biholomorphism.
Given the published double-Kodaira existence input and base hyperbolicity, the at-most-two bound is attained by two inequivalent Kodaira fibrations.
